title: Primary decomposition and dimension bound for generalized eigenspaces
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], meaning every nonconstant polynomial in $K[T]$ has a root in $K$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and let $T:V\to V$ be $K$-linear. For $a\in K$ define the generalized eigenspace $E_a(T)=\{v\in V:\text{there exists }n\geq0\text{ with }(T-a\,\mathrm{id}_V)^n v=0\}$. The family $(E_a(T))_{a\in K}$ is an internal direct sum with sum $V$: every vector has a unique expression as a finitely supported sum $\sum_a v_a$ with $v_a\in E_a(T)$. Moreover, writing $d=\dim_K V$, one has $E_a(T)=\ker((T-a\,\mathrm{id}_V)^d)$ for every $a\in K$. This includes $V=0$, where $d=0$ and every $E_a(T)=0$.

Together these say precisely that finite sums are unique and exhaust V. The dimension bound is Module.End.maxGenEigenspace_eq_genEigenspace_finrank at Basic.lean:602-607. The definitions agree directly by Module.End.mem_maxGenEigenspace at Basic.lean:551-552 and Module.End.mem_genEigenspace_nat at Basic.lean:91-92. Fields are domains and vector spaces torsion-free, so the independence theorem applies. For V=0 its dimension is zero and the kernel of the identity is zero.
